**2. Lab Notebook Excerpt – Dr. Sarah Chen**
**Notebook ID: SC-2020-01, Entry #14**
**Date: 2020-04-22 (SGT)**
**Location: Physics Block S13, Lab 03-12**

Setup for the 800 nm Ti:Sapphire amplifier (LSA-01) was modified to improve beam pointing stability. Replaced the periscope mirrors (M1, M2) with new silver-coated optics; old gold mirrors showed significant astigmatism after 6 months of high-average-power operation. Measured the beam profile using the WinCamD at the sample plane: 1/e² diameter = 4.2 mm (x) × 4.1 mm (y), which is acceptable for the BBO doubling stage.

For the SHG autocorrelation, I used a 100 µm BBO crystal (θ = 29.2°). The spectrum of the fundamental was centered at 800 nm with a FWHM of 45 nm. Autocorrelation trace (interferometric) showed a pulse duration of 32 fs (assuming sech²). This is slightly longer than the expected 28 fs; I suspect the compressor gratings are misaligned. Will re-check grating angle tomorrow.

*Note to self:* The new spectrometer (Ocean Optics HR4000) has a lower noise floor, but the integration time needs to be set to at least 10 ms to avoid saturation when using the fiber bundle. For the white-light continuum generation experiment, I will use a 2 mm sapphire plate instead of the usual 3 mm. The shorter path length should reduce the spectral modulation we saw last week.

---

**3. Lab Notebook Excerpt – Dr. Sarah Chen**
**Notebook ID: SC-2020-02, Entry #07**
**Date: 2020-08-14 (SGT)**
**Location: Physics Block S13, Lab 03-12**

Ran a series of measurements to characterize the supercontinuum generated in a 5 cm YAG crystal. Pumped with 1.2 mJ, 35 fs pulses at 1 kHz. The spectrum extended from 450 nm to 1600 nm (limited by the InGaAs detector). The shot-to-shot stability was poor (σ = 8% over 100 shots). I suspect thermal lensing in the crystal is the culprit. To mitigate, I will mount the crystal on a copper block with better thermal contact. Alternatively, I can use a rotating holder, but the motor adds vibration.

In the lab notebook, Dr. Sarah Chen has_research_focus nonlinear optics. Record status: current.

We also tested the new 2D-SPIDER setup. The calibration was successful; the retrieved spectral phase was flat to within 50 mrad over the central 60 nm. The main issue is the alignment of the two replicas; the shear was set to 2.4 nm, which is acceptable. The data acquisition time is still slow (5 s per acquisition), but this is fine for now.

---

**4. Lab Notebook Excerpt – Dr. Sarah Chen**
**Notebook ID: SC-2021-01, Entry #03**
**Date: 2021-02-10 (SGT)**
**Location: Physics Block S13, Lab 03-12**

First successful demonstration of the mid-IR DFG source. We used a 1 mm GaSe crystal (type I, ooe) to mix the signal and idler from our OPA (TOPAS). The OPA was pumped with 4 mJ of the fundamental; signal at 1.3 µm, idler at 2.0 µm. The DFG output was centered at 3.6 µm with a bandwidth of 150 nm (FWHM). The average power was 12 mW at 1 kHz repetition rate. This is a promising result for our planned spectroscopy experiments.

The main challenge is the poor beam quality (M² = 2.5). I believe this is due to the walk-off in the GaSe crystal. We will try a different crystal orientation or a collinear geometry to improve the spatial profile. Also, the long-term stability is not great; the power drifts by 5% over 30 minutes. This might be due to absorption in the crystal causing thermal effects.

One point of concern raised by the internal reviewer was the stability of the DFG source; we have addressed this by proposing a temperature-stabilized crystal mount and a power feedback loop.

**Date: 2021-10-05 (SGT)**
**Location: Physics Block S13, Lab 03-12**

The dual-comb setup is now on the optical table. I spent most of the day aligning the two DFG stages. The first stage produces the signal comb; the second stage is pumped by the idler from the same OPA. The idler has a broad spectrum, so I had to insert a bandpass filter (3.5–3.7 µm) in the second stage to ensure the two combs have overlapping spectra. This filter reduces the idler power from 80 mW to 45 mW, but the second DFG still produces about 6 mW of average power at 3.6 µm. Good enough for a first test.

The beat-note measurement is tricky. I used a fast InGaAs detector (12 GHz bandwidth) and a spectrum analyzer. The beat note appears at 250 MHz, which matches the difference in repetition rates between the two combs. However, the signal is weak; the SNR is only about 15 dB. I suspect the issue is the timing jitter between the two DFG stages. The OPA has some pulse-to-pulse energy fluctuation, which translates into timing jitter in the DFG process. We may need to add a feedback loop on the pump energy.

Tomorrow I will try to lock the beat note to a reference oscillator using a PLL. If that works, we can proceed to the multipass cell.

Realigned the in-coupling optics for the Kagome fiber compressor. The throughput improved from 62% to 71%, which is close to the pre-move value of 73%. **2. Lab Notebook Excerpt – Dr. Sarah Chen**
**Notebook ID: SC-2020-01, Entry #14**
**Date: 2020-04-22 (SGT)**
**Location: Physics Block S13, Lab 03-12**

Setup for the 800 nm Ti:Sapphire amplifier (LSA-01) was modified to improve beam pointing stability. Replaced the periscope mirrors (M1, M2) with new silver-coated optics; old gold mirrors showed significant astigmatism after 6 months of high-average-power operation. Measured the beam profile using the WinCamD at the sample plane: 1/e² diameter = 4.2 mm (x) × 4.1 mm (y), which is acceptable for the BBO doubling stage.

For the SHG autocorrelation, I used a 100 µm BBO crystal (θ = 29.2°). The spectrum of the fundamental was centered at 800 nm with a FWHM of 45 nm. Autocorrelation trace (interferometric) showed a pulse duration of 32 fs (assuming sech²). This is slightly longer than the expected 28 fs; I suspect the compressor gratings are misaligned. Will re-check grating angle tomorrow.

*Note to self:* The new spectrometer (Ocean Optics HR4000) has a lower noise floor, but the integration time needs to be set to at least 10 ms to avoid saturation when using the fiber bundle. For the white-light continuum generation experiment, I will use a 2 mm sapphire plate instead of the usual 3 mm. The shorter path length should reduce the spectral modulation we saw last week.

---

**3. Lab Notebook Excerpt – Dr. Sarah Chen**
**Notebook ID: SC-2020-02, Entry #07**
**Date: 2020-08-14 (SGT)**
**Location: Physics Block S13, Lab 03-12**

Ran a series of measurements to characterize the supercontinuum generated in a 5 cm YAG crystal. Pumped with 1.2 mJ, 35 fs pulses at 1 kHz. The spectrum extended from 450 nm to 1600 nm (limited by the InGaAs detector). The shot-to-shot stability was poor (σ = 8% over 100 shots). I suspect thermal lensing in the crystal is the culprit. To mitigate, I will mount the crystal on a copper block with better thermal contact. Alternatively, I can use a rotating holder, but the motor adds vibration.

In the lab notebook, Dr. Sarah Chen has_research_focus nonlinear optics. Record status: current.

We also tested the new 2D-SPIDER setup. The calibration was successful; the retrieved spectral phase was flat to within 50 mrad over the central 60 nm. The main issue is the alignment of the two replicas; the shear was set to 2.4 nm, which is acceptable. The data acquisition time is still slow (5 s per acquisition), but this is fine for now.

---

**4. Lab Notebook Excerpt – Dr. Sarah Chen**
**Notebook ID: SC-2021-01, Entry #03**
**Date: 2021-02-10 (SGT)**
**Location: Physics Block S13, Lab 03-12**

First successful demonstration of the mid-IR DFG source. We used a 1 mm GaSe crystal (type I, ooe) to mix the signal and idler from our OPA (TOPAS). The OPA was pumped with 4 mJ of the fundamental; signal at 1.3 µm, idler at 2.0 µm. The DFG output was centered at 3.6 µm with a bandwidth of 150 nm (FWHM). The average power was 12 mW at 1 kHz repetition rate. This is a promising result for our planned spectroscopy experiments.

The main challenge is the poor beam quality (M² = 2.5). I believe this is due to the walk-off in the GaSe crystal. We will try a different crystal orientation or a collinear geometry to improve the spatial profile. Also, the long-term stability is not great; the power drifts by 5% over 30 minutes. This might be due to absorption in the crystal causing thermal effects.

**7. Lab Notebook Excerpt – Dr. Kelvin Ng**
**Notebook ID: KN-2021-02, Entry #11**
**Date: 2021-10-05 (SGT)**
**Location: Physics Block S13, Lab 03-12**

The dual-comb setup is now on the optical table. I spent most of the day aligning the two DFG stages. The first stage produces the signal comb; the second stage is pumped by the idler from the same OPA. The idler has a broad spectrum, so I had to insert a bandpass filter (3.5–3.7 µm) in the second stage to ensure the two combs have overlapping spectra. This filter reduces the idler power from 80 mW to 45 mW, but the second DFG still produces about 6 mW of average power at 3.6 µm. Good enough for a first test.

The beat-note measurement is tricky. I used a fast InGaAs detector (12 GHz bandwidth) and a spectrum analyzer. The beat note appears at 250 MHz, which matches the difference in repetition rates between the two combs. However, the signal is weak; the SNR is only about 15 dB. I suspect the issue is the timing jitter between the two DFG stages. The OPA has some pulse-to-pulse energy fluctuation, which translates into timing jitter in the DFG process. We may need to add a feedback loop on the pump energy.

Tomorrow I will try to lock the beat note to a reference oscillator using a PLL. If that works, we can proceed to the multipass cell.

**26. Group Meeting Minutes – 2022-07-25**
**Attendees: Dr. Tan (PI), Dr. Kumar, Dr. Ng, Dr. Chen, M. Lim (PhD student)**
**Location: Physics Block S13, Meeting Room 04-01**
**Time: 14:00–15:15 SGT**

Agenda items and summary:

1. **Mid-IR source status (Dr. Ng).** The PLL lock on the beat note was achieved on 2022-07-04. Dr. Ng reports stable locking over 4 hours with residual phase noise below 200 mrad integrated from 10 Hz to 1 MHz. The timing jitter issue from the DFG stages appears mitigated. The multipass cell is now being commissioned. Dr. Kumar asked whether the pump energy fluctuation at the 1 kHz repetition rate was fully addressed; Dr. Ng clarified that the feedback loop on pump energy is still under test and will be validated by measuring the out-of-loop timing jitter with a cross-correlator. Target is jitter < 5 fs over 1 hour.

2. **Hollow-core fiber compressor (Dr. Chen).** The Kagome fiber setup from the previous quarter has been moved to the new optical table in Lab 2. Dr. Chen reports a 10% loss in throughput after the move, likely due to a slight misalignment of the in-coupling lens. A realignment is scheduled for this week. The compressed pulse duration remains 5 fs as measured by d-scan; no degradation observed.

3. **Thermal lensing study (Dr. Kumar).** The paper on thermal lensing in high-average-power mid-IR crystals was published in Applied Physics B in April. Dr. Kumar is now extending the study to orientation-patterned GaAs (OP-GaAs) specifically for the high-energy DFG source. He presented preliminary finite-element simulations showing a 15% reduction in thermal lensing when using a diamond heat spreader. M. Lim will assist with the experimental validation using a Hartmann sensor. The group agreed to target a conference submission to CLEO 2023 with these results.

4. **Grant proposal update (Dr. Tan).** The group discussed the upcoming call from the Ministry of Education (MOE) AcRF Tier 2. Dr. Tan will lead a proposal on "High-energy, carrier-envelope-phase-stable mid-infrared sources for strong-field physics." A white paper draft is due to the department research office by 2022-08-15. Dr. Ng and Dr. Chen will contribute sections on the DFG source and the pulse compression, respectively. Dr. Kumar will contribute to the thermal management section. Dr. Tan reminded everyone that the university requires all external collaborators to be listed with their institutional email addresses for the submission.

5. **A.O.B.** M. Lim asked about the schedule for the multipass cell experiments. Dr. Ng indicated that the first full characterization is planned for early September. Dr. Tan also reminded the group of the upcoming safety inspection of Lab 2 on 2022-08-05.

Meeting adjourned at 15:15 SGT. Next meeting: 2022-08-22.

**27. Laboratory Notebook Entry – Dr. S. Chen**
**Date: 2022-08-03**
**Location: Lab 2, Physics Block S13**

Realigned the in-coupling optics for the Kagome fiber compressor. The throughput improved from 62% to 71%, which is close to the pre-move value of 73%. The residual 2% loss is attributed to a slight ellipticity of the beam from the newly installed periscope. I will check the periscope mirror mounts tomorrow.

After the realignment, I re-measured the compressed pulse duration using the d-scan device. The result was 5.2 fs, which is within the measurement uncertainty of the previous 5 fs value. The spectral phase was flat to within 50 mrad over the full bandwidth.

I also noticed a slight drift in the output beam pointing over 2 hours. The drift is about 20 µrad, likely due to thermal expansion of the optical table. I will add a beam-pointing stabilisation stage (two mirror mounts with piezo actuators) to the setup next week. The parts are already ordered.
